title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: The Company's Directors and those employees directly reporting to the Managing Director. This Policy applies only to KMP (there is no separate, lighter regime for other employees); subject to Closed Periods, the approval/notification regime, the no-short-term-trading rule, and the disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: must obtain the prior approval of the Board itself, rather than of the Chairman, before buying, selling or exercising rights.

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: Distinguished as the officer who determines severe financial hardship/exceptional circumstances applications from other KMP for a Closed Period exemption; where the Managing Director is the applicant, the determination is instead made by all other members of the Board.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates of a KMP, such as family members, family trusts and family companies. The insider trading prohibition and the notification obligation in 5.3 both extend to dealings by a KMP through an Associate.

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's Annual Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Company's Annual Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Half Year Financial Report of the Company
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Half Year Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Company's quarterly reports

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion vary the Closed Period rule in relation to a particular Closed Period, by general announcement to all Key Management Personnel either before or during that Closed Period; as a general announcement, this is not framed as confidential.

rules.detail: The Policy's operative concept is limited to buying, selling or exercising rights in Company securities (clauses 2, 3.1, 5.1); derivatives, hedges or other financial products are never mentioned.
No hedging restriction, definition, or reference of any kind appears in the Policy.
Monetisation structures (e.g. prepaid forwards) are not addressed; the Policy does not define dealing to include agreements to deal in the future, only actual buying, selling or exercising of rights.
Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named anywhere in the Policy.

Entering a margin lending arrangement is not itself a 'buy, sell or exercise rights' transaction and so falls outside the approval/notification regime; the Policy affirmatively contemplates such arrangements by naming 'margin lending arrangement' as an example of secured lender rights and by excusing a resulting forced sale from insider trading and Closed Period restrictions.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage or charge over Company securities held is not a 'buy, sell or exercise rights' transaction and so is not covered by the approval regime; the Policy expressly contemplates such security being given and confirms a subsequent forced sale on default does not itself breach insider trading laws.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: No prohibition, clearance requirement or disclosure obligation applies to entering a secured financing arrangement over Company securities; only the resulting forced sale on default is addressed, and it is treated as compliant and excluded from Closed Period restrictions.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: General ban on short-term trading, with a single carve-out for exercising options where the resulting shares are sold shortly thereafter (e.g. a cash/cashless exercise).
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chairman wishes to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities, the Chairman must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire ordinary shares in the Company by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares.
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class.
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class.
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules).
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Key Management Personnel in an employee incentive scheme ... where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that scheme.
acquire ordinary shares in the Company as a result of the exercise of options held under an employee option scheme.
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary.

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person.
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer.

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a prohibited period.
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or all other members of the Board if the applicant is the Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: Key Management Personnel may be in severe financial hardship if they have a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied other than by selling the securities of the Company.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or all other members of the Board if the applicant is the Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company securities by a Key Management Personnel if the person is required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking for example in a bona fide family settlement, to transfer or sell securities of the Company, or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.

exemption_authority: The Managing Director (or, where the applicant is the Managing Director, all other members of the Board) may grant written clearance for a KMP not in possession of inside information to sell or dispose of Company securities during a Closed Period, based on a written application with supporting documentation showing severe financial hardship or a court order/overriding legal requirement; any exemption issued is in writing and specifies the time period during which the sale may be made (5.5-5.8).

bespoke_clauses.topic: narrow dealing concept excludes derivatives and financing
bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company ... Any Key Management Personnel ... wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because the Policy's approval, notification and Closed Period regime is keyed only to buying, selling or exercising rights, entering an OTC put/call collar, or the loan securing it, is arguably outside the Policy's operative scope altogether, subject always to the overriding insider trading law.

bespoke_clauses.topic: mortgage/charge and forced sale expressly contemplated
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy affirmatively contemplates the shares being pledged as security and treats the lender's enforcement sale as compliant and excluded from Closed Period restrictions, favouring the secured-loan leg of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling a collar by a large share sale (over 10% of the executive's holding or of 20-day ADV) triggers a mandatory pre-sale discussion with the Board and lawyers, an added process step though not a prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.topic: option exercise price funded by share sale
bespoke_clauses.clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar or its funding is linked to an option exercise, any cashless-exercise sale to fund the exercise price must occur outside a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Associates bound by same notification duty
bespoke_clauses.clause: any Key Management Personnel who (or through his or her Associates) buys, sells, or exercises rights in relation to Company securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of the transaction within two (2) business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a sale through a family member, family trust or family company does not avoid the notification duty, though it also does not create any additional restriction beyond that duty.

summary: This 2018-era policy's only defined 'dealing' concept is buying, selling or exercising rights in Company securities; it contains no restriction on derivatives, hedging, CFDs, short selling or securities lending, so an OTC put/call collar over vested shares is not addressed and, on its narrow wording, appears to fall outside the Policy's operative scope (subject always to the overriding insider trading law). The loan leg is expressly contemplated and favourable: clause 4.4(b) confirms that providing Company securities as security by mortgage or charge does not itself breach insider trading law, and 4.4(a)(xii) treats a secured lender's enforcement sale on default as an exception available at any time, including during a Closed Period, without further clearance. Key Management Personnel must still obtain prior written approval from the Chairman (or the Board, for the Chairman) before any buy, sell or exercise of rights, notify the Company Secretary within two business days, avoid dealing during the twice-yearly and quarterly Closed Periods or while holding inside information, and avoid short-term trading. A sale used to unwind or settle the collar exceeding 10% of the executive's holding or of 20-day average volume must be discussed with the Board and the Company's lawyers before execution. Both legs of a funded collar appear achievable on this policy's own terms, though the drafting predates any express treatment of derivatives, so written confirmation from the Company via the ordinary clearance process is advisable before proceeding.
